We started seeing a sharp increase in 429s and 500-level retries against the Redwood endpoint at ~14:40 PDT (request IDs attached). Latency has doubled for most of our realtime inference calls; a few jobs are timing out. This started right after our peak morning traffic.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 4 Aug 2028 16:05:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 429s + latency increase — BlueFjord

Triage notes (short):
- Root cause appears to be a policy math mismatch introduced during a policy migration we ran earlier this week. The tenant-level burst credits (request-count-based) were left in place, but we also activated a new tokenized quota layer (token-count-based) that counts both prompt + generation tokens differently. For certain payloads (long prompt + long generation) the system double-applied suppression heuristics.
- Result: the real-time governor hit a conservative suppression threshold and started returning token-based 429 responses; simultaneously the per-tenant burst window consumed credits faster than intended because request != token accounting.

Immediate mitigation plan (what we will do in the next 60 minutes):
1) Apply an emergency policy override for tenant BF-1742 to lift token-based suppression for 30 minutes (temporary). See console steps in console-override-instructions.md (attached).
2) SRE to add 10% headroom to the Dedicated pool serving BlueFjord to absorb the queued requests (Connor).
3) Recompute burst-credit allocation to avoid double-counting and deploy a small patch to the policy engine within 6 hours (policy-diff-20280804.patch attached).

Longer term: we need a postmortem and an audit of migration tooling. I’ll own remediate + roll-forward tests.

Logs attached: redwood-prelim-logs-20280804.zip

—
Karthik Iyer
Lead, Quota & Policy — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Marissa / MarComm / Ops,

Summary: BlueFjord (BF-1742) experienced production throttling yesterday afternoon due to a misapplied quota/burst migration. We identified a policy accounting mismatch that caused token-based suppression to be applied in addition to existing burst credits, effectively double-counting high-cost requests. Karthik’s team has a short mitigation path (temporary override + small capacity bump) and a patch to correct the math.

Customer impact: approximately 15–20% 429 rate during the 14:38–14:46 window; latency increased 1.8x for realtime endpoints. BlueFjord is requesting an immediate ETA and customer credits for business impact. They are a mid-enterprise health customer on a committed Dedicated plan (monthly commit).

Ask (requires exec sign-off):
1) Approve a temporary Dedicated pool headroom allocation for BlueFjord for 24 hours to ensure no further customer-facing errors. Estimated incremental cloud cost: ~$3,200/day.
2) Approve a one-time customer credit for the affected billing window (suggested credit: 10% of July invoice or equivalent $ value). We recommend approval given production impact and mission-critical workload.
3) Public statement: permission to share a short incident note and our remediation plan with BlueFjord CS by EOD today.

We have the technical mitigations ready: policy override steps and patch to policy engine. If we get green on (1) and (2) I’ll coordinate communications and confirm rollback criteria.

Cc: Connor — can you confirm ETA for capacity bump and whether we can make the override without a broader risk to adjacent tenants?

Sofia
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
